B35.capture_spec: C13: 11-door.gdshader with pivot (-64, 0) x U on the card; card texture drawn at 1024 px (U = 8 times the 128 px card; a clean cream card, warm grey border, teal arrow pointing right, small teal square top left), node scale k/8 with k = 2.0 in a 1280x720 logical canvas, every pixel-valued uniform multiplied by U; a terracotta dot (radius 6 logical px) at the pivot, placed at the card's left edge midpoint; 4K SubViewport route, Forward+, 30 fps, offline fixed tick, no input; 15 s. flip keyframes: 0.0 from 0.00 to 0.10, 0.15 at 0.36 (ease), hold 0.15. At the 50 % and 85 % marks: the card at 54 degrees, its left edge at the hinge dot. Verified: left edge stays at -64; right edge at -64 + 128 cos (geometry-summary.txt).
B35.visual_intent: Act title 'The Pivot' (serif 40) top-left. A framed Godot window: the card swings like a door about its LEFT edge, a terracotta dot marks that edge (the hinge) and does not move while the rest of the card narrows toward it. Readout 'pivot' beside the dot; the caption reads 'pivot: the point it turns around'.
B35.motion_claim: The card swings about its left edge; the terracotta hinge dot never moves.

show.event: card at rest, hinge dot on its left edge
card swings to a door-ajar pose about the hinge

B35.why: The target look first: a real door-like swing with a fixed hinge dot makes 'pivot' something the viewer can see.

B36.visual_intent: The screen-direction grid with a small cross at the origin and a card whose left edge carries a terracotta pivot dot. Step 1 (label '1 slide in'): the card slides so that the pivot dot lands on the origin cross. Step 2 ('2 turn'): the card's width narrows and widens about the origin (a flip). Step 3 ('3 slide back'): the card slides back by the same amount, and the pivot dot returns to its original place; label 'the pivot never moved'.
B36.motion_claim: The card slides so the hinge dot sits on the origin, flips there, then slides back to where it was.

show.event: card with its pivot dot, origin cross
step 1: the card slides; dot on the cross
step 2: the card flips about the cross
step 3: the card slides back; dot home

B36.why: Three steps in order is a short animation; the card visibly travelling in, turning and travelling back is the claim.

props.caption: read it from the right

B37.visual_intent: A full-frame code card with the real six-line vertex function (the product written over three lines, one table per line). Focus climbs the product from the bottom line (slide in) to the middle (turn) to the top (slide back), then all three lines glow together.
B37.motion_claim: Focus climbs the three lines from the bottom up, the way the point meets the tables.
B37.why: The reading order runs bottom to top; LectureCodeTrace's focus only moves downward, so this needs ShaderLab's free line cues.
